problems: These tools are left out of this turn; tell the user, and fix the configuration when you can:
config:
Configures this chat page, which has no settings panel: its endpoints, model, system prompt, tools, display, style and every other setting. It runs lines of the KiSS CLI, one command per line; all lines of one call apply together or not at all, so batch related changes in a single call. Changes apply at once to the running configuration, and a call answers with what changed: the old line after -, the new one after +. Only the user keeps configuration changes, by typing /save <name>; load <name> goes back to a save, reset back to the site defaults: tell them so once such a change looks right.
Commands: set <module> <key> [name] <value> | no <module> <key> [name] | no <module> <name> | show <module> [key] [name] | show <module> <name> | show running | show models | show style | show saves | show diff <save> <save> | load <save> | reset | title <title> | show title | show conversations | export [<id>|all] | import. A save is a name; show diff reads session as the running configuration. title renames this conversation when the user asks; the conversation keeps its title, so a title needs no save. show conversations lists the conversations by id; export offers the user a file of this conversation, of another by its id, or of all; import asks the user for a file and adds the conversations it holds that are not here yet; neither changes a conversation, and each runs alone on its line.
A key is two fixed words, a module then a key; a key of a collection such as endpoints takes the item name next; the value always comes last. A line that stops short lists what may follow it: set lists the modules, set display its keys. show models lists the models of every endpoint, by endpoint, with their settings; set chat model takes a name as it lists it. Each model has its own request parameters, sent only when set: set models <temperature|top_p|top_k|min_p|max_tokens|presence_penalty|frequency_penalty|seed|reasoning_effort> <model> <value>, reasoning_effort being what the template of the model reads. set tools rounds caps the tool rounds of a turn; set endpoints timeout <name> and set mcp timeout <name> give each server its seconds. set display thinking|tools closed, open or inference, open while the model writes them. An MCP server, set mcp url <name> <url> and its bearer set mcp key <name>, gives you its tools; show tools lists every tool by who serves it; set tools use <name> off hides one, consent asks the user at each call, on lets it run. Some changes ask the user first: the url of an endpoint or an MCP server, chat model, chat system, and opening a tool; a refused change stays refused, never reach it another way; privilege, how far you change each module, is the user's. To give a key, write the line without its value, set mcp key <name>: the user types it in a field of their own, so never ask them to paste a key in the chat. show style lists the style of the page, its tokens under :root (show style | include :root); set css sheet <name> <css> restyles anything over it, the sheets applied by name, so one sheet holds one change. Words abbreviate (sh run) as long as one word only starts so. Filter any output with | include <pattern>. Quote values holding blanks.
Example call:
set css sheet accent ':root { --accent: oklch(0.62 0.21 300) }'
set endpoints url pod http://localhost:8080/v1
show css
